correctness.rationale: For any full-dimensional K in R^3, the even surface-area measure nu has mass S(partial K) supported on the finite projective facet normals. The weak projected-area domination is a cosine-transform inequality. The nonnegative even degree-2m polynomial g=product_i(1-(u.v_i)^2) vanishes on nu. Funk-Hecke eigenvalues at even degree 2k are nonzero, lambda_0=2pi and lambda_2k=(-1)^(k+1)4pi(2k-2)!/[4^k(k-1)!(k+1)!]. Finite spherical harmonic inversion Tq=g and the addition bound ||q||inf<=H_m make r=1/(2pi)-epsilon_m q positive and Tr=1-epsilon_m g. Integrating gives epsilon_m int g dmu <=2delta. Projective angular separation g>=rho^2 sin^(2m-2)(Delta/2) yields the boxed bound and Chebyshev the beta tail. Replacing an area-a facet patch by symmetric tilted patches of total area a sec(theta) preserves ALL cosine projection inequalities, delta~a theta^2/2 and angular moment~2a theta^2, showing the small-angle exponent 2 is optimal only for weak barriers. Exactly thirteen Legendre moments in the inspected verification source agree with the factorial formula; bounded grids alone are not the infinite proof.
